slides.title: Towards Agentic Agent-based Models: Feasibility, Performance, and Statistical Model Checking
slides.tldr: INTEGRATING LLM-BASED AGENTS INTO ABM SIMULATIONS
slides.highlight: This research explores the feasibility and reliability of replacing symbolic rules in agent-based models with LLM-driven decisions, which is relevant to MIMIC's use of LLM-based agent models for societal-scale simulation.

card.one_liner: Investigates the feasibility and impact of replacing symbolic ABM decision rules with LLM-based tool calls.
card.key_idea: Extends the Schelling segregation model in Mesa by delegating one agent's neighbor classification to a local LLM using tool-calling mechanisms.
card.evaluation: Evaluated using Qwen3.5 models (0.8b to 9b) via robustness checks and statistical model checking with MultiVeStA to compare trajectories.
card.limitation: Smaller LLMs exhibit semantic and operational failures; larger models introduce significant runtime overhead without changing model dynamics.

slides.title: MeetingToM: Evaluating Multimodal LLMs on Theory-of-Mind Reasoning in Multi-Party Meetings
slides.tldr: BENCHMARK FOR THEORY-OF-MIND REASONING IN MULTI-PARTY MEETINGS
slides.highlight: This work introduces MeetingToM to evaluate MLLMs on subject-level mental states, addressee understanding, and group consensus, aligning with HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception and listener modeling.

card.one_liner: MeetingToM is a multimodal benchmark evaluating MLLMs' Theory-of-Mind reasoning in complex multi-party meeting scenarios.
card.key_idea: A hierarchical evaluation framework testing subject-level mental states, dyadic-level addressee/attitude inference, and group-level consensus reasoning, specifically targeting 'pseudo-consensus' where verbal agreement masks private dissent.
card.evaluation: Evaluated proprietary (GPT-5, Gemini-3 Pro) and open-source (Qwen) MLLMs using 1,800 clips from the AMI Corpus; humans significantly outperformed all models.
card.limitation: Limited to English-language meetings, short video segments (5s-50s) rather than full meetings, and lacks original participant self-reported mental states.

slides.title: How Reliable Are Multimodal Signals of Conversational State? Evidence from Remote Dyadic Collaborative Tasks
slides.tldr: EVALUATING MULTIMODAL SIGNALS FOR CONVERSATIONAL STATE
slides.highlight: This research evaluates the reliability of interactional, acoustic, and linguistic features for predicting cognitive load and power roles, contributing to HyECHO's goal of multimodal social perception of team states.

card.one_liner: Multimodal signals for conversational state often lack generalizability and reliability once speaker identity is controlled.
card.key_idea: A three-dimensional framework (prediction, generalizability, reliability) evaluated interaction, acoustic, and linguistic features using LODO, LOCO, and speaker-normalized ICC on the AVCAffe dataset.
card.evaluation: Tested on 53 dyads across 9 tasks using Random Forest. Metrics included CCC for cognitive load and macro F1 for power.
card.limitation: Conversational power prediction remained near chance; results are limited to Zoom-mediated dyadic interactions and task-level aggregation.

slides.title: A Digital Twin-Based Method for Evaluating Local Collective Tariffs in Distribution-Level Energy Systems
slides.tldr: DIGITAL TWIN EVALUATION OF ENERGY TARIFFS
slides.highlight: This work proposes a digital twin-based method using agent-based modeling to evaluate how user behavior and infrastructure interact with collective energy tariffs. It is relevant to MIMIC's focus on meso-scale simulation and the impact analysis of human-AI agent models in societal systems.

card.one_liner: A digital twin method for evaluating local collective tariffs in distribution-level energy systems.
card.key_idea: Integrates agent-based modeling of households, virtual aggregation via shared metering, and explicit tariff logic within a unified simulation environment.
card.evaluation: Applied to the Danish Local Collective Tariff using residential configurations with PV, batteries, and EVs; results show community-level cost reductions.
card.limitation: Outcomes are sensitive to the temporal alignment of consumption and generation, affecting cost neutrality across participants.

slides.title: Imitation of Arm Gestures by the Semi-Humanoid Robot NICO
slides.tldr: HUMAN ARM GESTURE IMITATION FOR SEMI-HUMANOID ROBOTS
slides.highlight: This research develops a system for the NICO robot to imitate human arm gestures using MediaPipe pose-estimation and analytical geometry, contributing to the study of embodied social robots and HRI for RwB.

card.one_liner: A system for the NICO robot to imitate human arm gestures using monocular RGB input.
card.key_idea: Combines MediaPipe pose and hand landmark extraction with analytical geometry to compute joint angles, which are then linearly mapped to NICO's specific motor configurations.
card.evaluation: Tested with six participants performing 11 poses across three viewing angles. Results show moderate accuracy for most joints, with MAEs between 10° and 34°.
card.limitation: High reconstruction error for forearm rotation (50.1° MAE) and sensitivity to complex poses, self-occlusions, and extreme wrist flexion.

slides.title: Learning Personalized Safety Interventions for Haptic Human-Robot Shared Control
slides.tldr: PERSONALIZED HAPTIC SAFETY INTERVENTIONS
slides.highlight: This work proposes a framework to learn user-preferred haptic safety interventions, supporting the MOSAIC goal of aligning human-AI intent and adapting to individual human proficiency.

card.one_liner: A framework to personalize haptic safety interventions in robot teleoperation using sparse user demonstrations.
card.key_idea: A Learning from Haptics (LfH) framework that optimizes Control Barrier Function (CBF) response gains via a differentiable QP layer to match user-preferred force feedback.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via AirSim hardware-in-the-loop simulations and real-world DJI Tello drone experiments using GP-interpolated preferences and force-matching metrics.
card.limitation: Not clearly stated.

slides.title: Stability and Comfort in Mobile Robot-Pedestrian Interactions
slides.tldr: SOCIAL NAVIGATION FOR NONHOLONOMIC MOBILE ROBOTS
slides.highlight: This research develops socially aware algorithms for nonholonomic mobile robots to improve pedestrian comfort and stability in crowds, contributing to the goals of RwB regarding human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: A socially-aware navigation framework for nonholonomic mobile robots that improves pedestrian comfort using a PTTC-based model.
card.key_idea: Implements a nonholonomic framework for Social Force Models (SFM) and a novel Projected Time-to-Collision SFM (TSFM) to imitate human-like movement while respecting kinematic constraints.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via simulations and real-world experiments comparing SFM and TSFM against remote-controlled baselines and DRL using speed and pedestrian comfort surveys.
card.limitation: TSFM improves pedestrian comfort but results in lower robot speeds compared to the standard SFM.

slides.title: Modeling turn-taking with distant viewing: investigating silence thresholds in human and AI-generated discourse
slides.tldr: SILENCE THRESHOLDS IN HUMAN AND AI DISCOURSE
slides.highlight: This study analyzes silence gaps in human and AI-generated audiovisual material, contributing to the understanding of turn-taking and engagement relevant to HyECHO.

card.one_liner: Study compares silence gaps in human sitcoms versus AI-generated podcasts to investigate turn-taking thresholds.
card.key_idea: Analysis of silence gaps across speaker gender and production settings using audiovisual material and fundamental-frequency thresholds estimated in Praat.
card.evaluation: Analyzed 30 US sitcoms and 51 Google NotebookLM synthetic podcasts; metrics focused on silence gap durations.
card.limitation: Not clearly stated.

slides.title: Motion Primitive Discovery in a Humanoid Robot via Self-Organising Maps for Phase Recognition
slides.tldr: MOTOR PRIMITIVE DISCOVERY VIA SOM AND ESN
slides.highlight: This work proposes an architecture for motor primitive discovery and online phase recognition in humanoid robots, which is relevant to RwB's focus on human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: A two-level MNS-inspired architecture for online movement phase recognition in a humanoid robot.
card.key_idea: Two Self-Organising Maps (SOMs) extract arm and hand motion primitives, which an Echo State Network (ESN) then integrates temporally to recognize movement phases.
card.evaluation: Tested on 4,200 simulated NICO robot trials across seven actions. Achieved 93.9% phase recognition accuracy using only SOM primitives.
card.limitation: Trained and evaluated only on the robot's own actions; lacks cross-embodiment observation capabilities.

slides.title: Chinese AI Brand Launches World’s First Humanoid Robot Fight League
slides.tldr: HUMANOID ROBOT FIGHT LEAGUE
slides.highlight: The launch of a humanoid robot fight league provides insights into the physical capabilities and interaction dynamics of humanoid systems, relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots.

slides.title: SpEmoC: A Balanced Speaker-Segment Multimodal Emotion Benchmark
slides.tldr: MULTIMODAL EMOTION BENCHMARK FOR CONVERSATIONS
slides.highlight: This work introduces a balanced multimodal dataset for emotion recognition in spoken conversations, supporting HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception and engagement.

card.one_liner: SpEmoC is a balanced, large-scale multimodal emotion benchmark featuring synchronized video, audio, and text clips.
card.key_idea: A hybrid pipeline using pretrained models and human validation to curate 30k balanced clips from 3,100 movies, utilizing movie-level splits to ensure robust generalization.
card.evaluation: Evaluated five SOTA models (e.g., EMOE, TCL-MAP) via in-domain benchmarking and cross-dataset transfer with MELD and CAER; results show significantly reduced imbalance gaps.
card.limitation: Demographic attributes are approximate, inferred from visual content and potentially affected by makeup, lighting, or role-based appearance.

slides.title: Experiential Versus Instructional Approaches for Eliciting Metacognitive Awareness in AI-Assisted Learning
slides.tldr: EXPERIENTIAL LEARNING IMPROVES AI METACOGNITIVE REGULATION
slides.highlight: This study demonstrates that experiential learning enhances the regulation of cognition in AI-assisted contexts over time, providing insights for ADAM-CHAT's focus on meta-cognition and self-correction.

card.one_liner: Experiential learning outperforms instructional approaches in immediately boosting AI-assisted metacognitive knowledge and student engagement.
card.key_idea: A quasi-experiment comparing hands-on experiential exercises (productive/unproductive AI use) against traditional lectures to measure metacognitive knowledge (MKC) and regulation (MRC) over five weeks.
card.evaluation: 126 first-year engineering students; measured via MAI-AI questionnaire at three timepoints. Results show significant immediate gains for experiential learning, though groups converged over time.
card.limitation: Immediate knowledge gains did not instantly translate to regulatory skills, and between-group differences in long-term regulation were not statistically significant.

slides.authors: Pau Benazet i Montobbio et al.

slides.title: Factorized Spatio-Temporal Convolutions for Human Pose Estimation from Planar Lidar
slides.tldr: HUMAN POSE ESTIMATION FROM PLANAR LIDAR
slides.highlight: This work presents a lightweight network for human detection and 2D pose estimation using planar LiDAR, supporting socially aware human-robot interaction for RwB.

card.one_liner: A lightweight network for omnidirectional human detection and 2D pose estimation using planar LiDAR sequences.
card.key_idea: Uses Space-Time Blocks (ST-Blocks) to factorize circular spatial convolutions and temporal convolutions, trained via cross-modal self-supervision from a narrow-FOV RGB-D body tracker.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on a custom dataset (OptiTrack ground truth) and FROG benchmark; outperformed parameter-matched baseline, reducing distance error by 38% and position error by 28%.
card.limitation: Cannot predict multiple people on the same ray; orientation estimation remains challenging due to inherent planar LiDAR ambiguity.

slides.title: Unified Prediction and Planning via Conflict-Aware Disjoint Parameter Training
slides.tldr: CONFLICT-AWARE DISJOINT PARAMETER TRAINING FOR ROBOT NAVIGATION
slides.highlight: This work proposes a framework to resolve representational conflicts between motion prediction and safety planning, enabling more efficient social robot navigation in crowded environments. It is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: DPT enables compact unified robot navigation models to perform prediction and planning without representational task conflicts.
card.key_idea: Disjoint Parameter Training (DPT) separates task-specific learning regions via binary masks, followed by Sparse Merging of only the most influential parameters to prevent interference.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on JRDB and JTA benchmarks using ADE, FDE, Collision Rate, and Miss Rate; outperformed DIPP, DTPP, and various merging baselines.
card.limitation: Not clearly stated.

slides.title: SOPD-SocialNav: Selective On-Policy Distillation for Vision-Language Social Navigation
slides.tldr: LIGHTWEIGHT VLM FOR SOCIAL NAVIGATION
slides.highlight: This work introduces a distillation method to transfer social navigation knowledge from large VLMs to lightweight models, supporting the development of socially aware embodied agents for RwB.

card.one_liner: SOPD-SocialNav distills social navigation knowledge from large VLMs to lightweight ones using selective on-policy distillation.
card.key_idea: Uses teacher uncertainty (entropy) to identify socially informative tokens and aligns student-teacher distributions via a temperature-controlled Jensen-Shannon divergence objective to avoid mode collapse.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on SNEI and MUSON benchmarks against SFT and KD baselines; results show superior action accuracy and reasoning consistency. Real-world Scout Mini tests confirm feasibility.
card.limitation: Real-world system throughput is low (0.365 FPS) due to network communication and image processing latency.

slides.title: Otap: Structure-Aware Optimal Transport for Evaluating Planning and Execution in Agent Trajectories
slides.tldr: STRUCTURE-AWARE OPTIMAL TRANSPORT FOR AGENT TRAJECTORY EVALUATION
slides.highlight: This work introduces a pseudo-metric using unbalanced fused Gromov-Wasserstein transport to evaluate agent trajectories, aligning with MOSAIC's use of Optimal Transport for intent alignment.

card.one_liner: Otap evaluates agent trajectories by measuring the structural and semantic distance between execution graphs using optimal transport.
card.key_idea: It uses an unbalanced fused Gromov-Wasserstein objective to align attributed dependency graphs, ensuring invariance to valid reorderings and robustness to hallucinations or granularity shifts.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via controlled perturbations and benchmarks (PlanBench, WebArena, GAIA). It outperformed semantic/lexical baselines in separating valid from invalid trajectories, especially with exact dependency graphs.
card.limitation: Performance drops when dependency graphs must be inferred heuristically from free-text traces rather than extracted from explicit semantics.

slides.title: AgentDebugX: An Open-Source Toolkit for Failure Observability, Attribution, and Recovery in LLM Agents
slides.tldr: LLM AGENT DEBUGGING FRAMEWORK
slides.highlight: AgentDebugX provides a closed-loop system for root-cause diagnosis and recovery in LLM agents, supporting the self-monitoring and self-correction goals of ADAM-CHAT.

card.one_liner: AgentDebugX is an open-source toolkit for detecting, attributing, and recovering from LLM agent failures.
card.key_idea: DeepDebug uses a multi-turn process (global read, structure-guided investigation, and cross-examination) to localize root causes and propose actionable fixes.
card.evaluation: Tested on Who&When (attribution) and GAIA (recovery); achieved 28.8% strict accuracy on Who&When and improved GAIA accuracy from 55.8% to 63.6%.
card.limitation: Pattern-based redaction cannot guarantee removal of all sensitive content when sharing bundles via the Error Hub.

slides.title: Differentiable Logic Programming to Mitigate Reasoning Shortcuts in Neurosymbolic Systems
slides.tldr: MITIGATING REASONING SHORTCUTS IN NEUROSYMBOLIC SYSTEMS
slides.highlight: This work proposes a differentiable logic programming method to reduce constraint satisfaction and cognition shortcuts in neurosymbolic systems, supporting MIMIC's use of neuro-symbolic agent models.

card.one_liner: A differentiable logic programming method to reduce reasoning shortcuts in neurosymbolic systems.
card.key_idea: Uses matrix-based logic programming with unified rule/constraint encoding and one-to-one grounding of neural outputs to logical atoms to prevent semantically incorrect mappings.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on MNIST variants; compared against soft probability distribution methods to show significant reduction in constraint satisfaction and cognition shortcuts.
card.limitation: Not clearly stated.

slides.title: Computational models of pragmatic reasoning with flexible generation of meaning and expression alternatives
slides.tldr: NEURO-SYMBOLIC FRAMEWORK FOR PRAGMATIC REASONING
slides.highlight: The SAGE framework combines language models with rule-based selectors to model how interlocutors reason over alternative expressions and interpretations, contributing to the understanding of social perception and listener modeling for HyECHO.

card.one_liner: SAGE combines language model flexibility with rule-based task analysis to model pragmatic reasoning over open-ended alternatives.
card.key_idea: A neuro-symbolic framework using LM-based 'proposers' for alternative generation, 'evaluators' for assessment, and 'selectors' for rule-based cognitive task implementation.
card.evaluation: Tested via three case studies (referential expressions, M-implicatures, Gricean implicatures) using ablations, baselines, and quantitative fit to human data.
card.limitation: LM evaluators struggle with formal/theoretical measures, performing better on intuitive judgments than on precise logical or semantic inference.

slides.title: Alibaba's Amap Unveils Full-Stack ABot Upgrade for Embodied AI Robots
slides.tldr: FULL-STACK ABOT UPGRADE FOR EMBODIED AI
slides.highlight: The unveiling of the ABot upgrade for embodied AI robots provides insights into full-stack systems relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots.

slides.title: Not Birds of a Feather: Personality-Based Partner Selection in LLM Agents
slides.tldr: PERSONALITY-BASED PARTNER SELECTION IN LLM AGENTS
slides.highlight: This research explores how LLM agents select partners based on Big Five personality traits, which is relevant to HyECHO's focus on modeling engagement and group norms in hybrid teams.

card.one_liner: LLM agents select partners based on task-personality stereotypes rather than capability or human-like similarity.
card.key_idea: Host agents chose partners from Big Five archetypes; selection followed task-trait maps (e.g., Openness for creativity) and favored complementarity over homophily, ignoring human performance benchmarks.
card.evaluation: Two studies (375 total trials) using Claude Haiku 4.5 agents across five task categories, validated via BFI-10 self-reports and blind LLM-judge ratings.
card.limitation: Used a single model family, simplified single-trait archetypes, and measured selection preferences rather than actual collaboration outcomes.

slides.title: Hazard or Anomaly? Evaluating VLMs for Understanding Dangers and Discrepancies
slides.tldr: EVALUATING VLM SAFETY REASONING
slides.highlight: This research distinguishes between hazards and anomalies in VLM scene interpretation, which is relevant to RwB's focus on human-robot interaction in safety-critical settings.

card.one_liner: VLMs often conflate unusual scene elements (anomalies) with actual physical dangers (hazards) in safety evaluations.
card.key_idea: Introduces a four-class taxonomy (Safe, Anomalous, Hazardous, Anomalous-Hazardous) and evaluates state-of-the-art VLMs using zero-shot, few-shot, and chain-of-thought prompting with images and dense captions.
card.evaluation: Tested 6 VLMs (GPT 4.1, Gemini, Mistral) on a 610-image benchmark using F1 scores and Hamming loss; results show hazards are easier to detect than anomalies.
card.limitation: Small dataset size (610 images) and subjectivity in non-expert annotations may limit the generality and statistical power of the results.
